title: Smith.ai: The AI Receptionist With a Human Net
meta: Honest Smith.ai review for 2026: real pricing (AI tiers + human virtual receptionist), why the human backup makes it the most reliable of the bunch, and the per-call cost creep to watch before you sign.
dek: If you're going to run an AI receptionist at all, this is the one that fails least — because it's a hybrid: AI answers, real humans catch what the bot drops. That reliability is also what makes the bill unpredictable. Here's the honest read before you hand it your phone.
verdict_text: If you must run AI, run this one. Smith.ai's human-backed hybrid is the most reliable of the AI receptionists — real agents escalate when the AI's out of its depth, so you get far fewer phantom bookings. The catch is per-call billing: transfers (~$3 each), add-ons, and spam calls make the monthly bill hard to predict. Still cheaper than a bad AI losing you a $9k job — but pricier than the boring $30 fix.

blocks.html: Most AI receptionists fail the same way: the moment a call goes off-script, the bot invents an answer or confirms a booking that never lands. Smith.ai's design hedges that — it's a hybrid. The AI handles the routine; real humans take over when it gets complicated. That single feature is why it earns the highest ratings in the category (G2 ~4.8, Capterra ~4.8, Trustpilot ~4.3) and why, if you're set on AI, it's the honest pick. It's not magic — it just doesn't leave a robot alone with your money.

faq.a: Of the AI receptionists, it's the most reliable because it's a hybrid — real humans escalate when the AI is out of its depth, so you get far fewer phantom bookings. It's worth testing (there's a free 25-call tier). The main downside is per-call billing, which makes the monthly cost unpredictable. Most small shops should still fix their own call response first.

The AI Receptionist has a free tier (25 calls/mo), then paid tiers around $150+ with per-call overage (~$2–$3) and ~$3 per AI-to-human transfer. The human virtual receptionist runs roughly $300–$2,100/mo at $7–$10 per call. Confirm current pricing on smith.ai.

faq.q: Is Smith.ai better than a pure AI receptionist?
faq.a: For reliability, yes — the human backup catches the off-script calls that cause phantom bookings and hallucinated answers in AI-only tools. You pay for that reliability through per-call billing, so watch transfer fees and spam-call volume.
